title: A cent left over by rounding the shares goes to the Labor row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 ($100.00), one part sold at $100.00 and a whole-invoice discount of $0.01; Labor reads {Sales-rep-A} and Parts reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  3. Read the discount share on the Labor row and on the Parts row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice is created.
  • Step 2: two rows show for the invoice.
  • Step 3: the two shares add up to exactly ($0.01), and the cent is on the Labor row: Labor ($0.01), Parts $0.00.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10890; story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative); PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R7, S5-R6, read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Each side's exact share is half a cent, so this tie lands on the Labor row under every reading of the rounding rule. How a share that is not a tie is rounded is a question for the product owner.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R7: “A cent left over by rounding the share goes to the Labor row.”
  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00.”
